q.t: Wet waste like food peels goes in which colour bin?
q.e: Green bin = wet waste — things that rot.

q.t: Dry waste like paper and plastic goes in which colour bin?
q.e: Blue bin = dry waste — things that don't rot.

q.t: Which tile gets hotter in the sun?
q.e: Black absorbs most sunlight and turns it into heat; white reflects it.

q.t: During a fire, under smoke you should…
o: Crawl low with your mouth covered
q.e: Smoke rises, so the cleanest air is near the floor.

q.t: After escaping a fire, you should…
q.e: Conditions change in seconds; going back is very dangerous.

q.t: With no footpath, you should walk…
o: In the middle of the road
q.e: Facing it, you can see vehicles coming and step aside.

q.t: Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya is about…
o: Clean toilets, safe water and hygiene in schools
q.e: It is part of the Swachh Bharat Mission for clean schools.

q.t: Old newspapers should be…
q.e: Recyclers buy them — a trade where both sides gain.

q.t: Ice stupas in Ladakh are…
o: Towers of ice that melt slowly in summer for water
q.e: They store winter water as ice and release it when needed.

q.t: Which keeps a room cool without electricity?
q.e: White reflects sunlight, so less of it becomes heat.

q.t: Why are water and electricity wasted so easily?
q.e: A dripping tap or fan in an empty room looks normal, so waste happens by default.

q.t: Why mix-ups of wet and dry waste are bad:
o: Then neither can be composted or recycled
q.e: Separated, both halves are useful; mixed, both are rubbish.

q.t: Who should separate waste?
o: The person throwing it, at that moment
q.e: Nobody can un-mix waste afterwards.

q.t: Why do explorer teams get specific questions instead of 'look around'?
o: A question tells you what to look for
q.e: Like scientists, you decide what you are observing for.

q.t: A dripping tap wastes a lot because…
o: It keeps dripping day and night
It drips only in school hours
q.e: The drop is tiny, but it repeats every second, even when nobody is there.

q.t: Which saves more water?
o: Turning the tap off while brushing for 2 minutes
q.e: A leak works all day and night; a brushing habit acts for two minutes.

q.t: Why is the air under a tree cooler than under a tin sheet?
o: Water evaporating from leaves takes heat away
q.e: A tree gives shade AND cools by evaporation.

q.t: Why practise fire drills when there's no fire?
o: It is a rule with no reason
q.e: In an emergency people do what they've done before.

q.t: Why shouldn't you hide in a bathroom during a fire?
o: Rescuers can't find you and there's no way out
q.e: Hiding traps you and hides you from rescuers.

q.t: A good school gate signboard should be…
o: Readable by a driver in one second
q.e: One clear message in few words or a symbol.

q.t: Why does white paint keep a roof cool?
o: It reflects sunlight so it never becomes heat
q.e: Light bounces away instead of being taken in.

q.t: A tree, a white roof and a good window are better than a fan because…
o: They keep working for years without electricity
They are cheaper to switch on
q.e: Design choices made once keep cooling for free.

q.t: Why do light-coloured clothes feel better in summer?
q.e: Like the white tile, light colours reflect much of the light.

q.t: Why tell staff at once if a classmate is missing after a fire?
o: Rescuers need to know who and where
q.e: A quick head count tells rescuers exactly whom to look for.

q.t: Why 'move quickly but do not run' in a fire drill?
o: Running causes falls and blocked doorways
q.e: Panic and pushing cause more harm than walking quickly.

q.t: A butterfly garden works because…
q.e: Plant the right flowers, and you give butterflies a reason to come.

q.t: Which question is most valuable after an investigation?
q.e: A surprise shows you had a belief that was wrong — that's where learning happens.

q.t: Why must sharp glass not be mixed with other waste?
q.e: Separating waste protects the people who handle it.

q.t: A friend scribbles on a bench and you only watch. What did your silence teach?
q.e: Behaviour spreads by example — the watcher matters as much as the doer.

q.t: The Jal Shakti Abhiyan is a campaign to…
q.e: It encourages planting trees, catching rainwater and using water wisely.

q.t: Two glasses of water: one under a tree, one in the sun. After an hour, the one in the sun is…
q.e: The tree's canopy stops sunlight before it reaches the glass.

q.t: A test before acting in public: would it be okay if…
q.e: One person cutting a queue barely matters; everyone doing it means there's no queue.

q.t: Why helmets for motorcyclists and miners?
q.e: Like other headgear, they have a practical protective job.

q.t: A green school starts with…
q.e: You can't fix what nobody has noticed.

q.t: Which is wet waste?
q.e: Wet waste is anything that rots.

q.t: Which is dry waste?
q.e: Dry waste doesn't rot — paper, plastic, glass, metal, cloth.

q.t: A row of trees along a street…
o: Lowers the temperature of the whole street
Only shades the strip under it
q.e: Shade plus evaporation cools the surrounding air.

q.t: Why help others in a fire only if it is safe?
o: A second person in danger helps nobody
q.e: If you get trapped too, rescuers have two people to save.

q.t: Which measure makes a school gate safer?
o: A marked crossing and staggered exit times
q.e: Fewer crowds, slower vehicles and marked crossings reduce danger.

q.t: Wet patches around school are a problem because…
q.e: Water watchers look for standing water where mosquitoes breed.
